findings.title: Mutable/stale default evaluated once at class definition time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the class is defined (module import time), not per-instance. All AssignmentSource instances created without explicitly passing `queued` will share the same timestamp (the time the module was imported), not the actual time the instance was created. This should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.

findings.title: to_dict/from_dict round-trip may fail on datetime serialization
findings.body: to_dict() uses dataclasses.asdict which keeps `queued` as a native datetime object. This dict is passed as `assignment_source_dict` through Celery task kwargs (sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async), which typically require JSON-serializable arguments depending on the serializer configured. If the task broker uses JSON serialization, a raw datetime will fail to serialize, breaking the outbound sync task entirely.

findings.title: where_should_sync doesn't pass sync_source to should_sync
findings.body: where_should_sync calls `.should_sync(key)` without threading through any AssignmentSource, so inbound-related sync checks here (e.g. inbound_assignee) can't filter cycles consistently with the new sync_source mechanism added elsewhere. This is inconsistent with the rest of the PR's goal and could still allow cycles for code paths going through this function with a source context ignored (not used anywhere currently, but is a latent inconsistency with the new API).
